messages:
incidents-bot: :rotating_light: ALERT: realtime latency anomaly detected for hosted-us-west1. p95 has jumped from ~180ms to ~1.2s and p99 to ~3.4s for text-generation endpoints. Error-rate stable but streaming stalls observed. Paging oncall.
oncall-rotation: i'm on it — digging into dashboards now. where's the link to the live p95/p99 graph? sending to #oncall-handoff if needed.
ana (sre): Dashboards -> https://dash.redwood.internal/d/latency/realtime?region=us-west1
ana (sre): quick glance: spike started ~1758002400, coincides with a small traffic surge from a single customer (cust-acme) + increased batch sizes on model-prod-v2.
julie (runtime): saw increased kv-cache misses from the same timeframe, and some raft of kv eviction logs around 1758002425. possible cache pressure causing repeated recompute for long sequences.
mike (infra): checking node-level metrics: several infer nodes in pool-uw1 show CPU waiting and >70% memcpy stalls. NVLink errors? logs pulled.
sam (eng-platform): I see three streaming workers reporting a stalled write loop — stacktrace points to send_pipeline blocking on socket flush after 60s. Could be backpressure from the streamer or client-side slow consumes.
customer-support: we have two customers already filing support tickets about slow chat responses — tagging them and asking for session ids.
ana (sre): immediate mitigations we can try in order: 1) disable batching for the affected model route 2) bump pool capacity by adding reserved nodes from the dedicated spare pool 3) route traffic for cust-acme to model-prod-v1 fallback variant 4) increase kv-cache TTL temporarily to reduce recompute.
oj: (bot) runbook suggestion: /runbook latency-spike -> recommended steps and rollback playbook.
oncall-rotation: executing step 1 now — turning off continuous batching on model-prod-v2 for us-west1.
julie (runtime): ack. disabling batching config: 
```
PATCH /api/config/models/model-prod-v2
{ "region_overrides": { "us-west1": { "batching": "off" } } }
```
julie (runtime): applying... response OK.
sam (eng-platform): starting capacity bump: adding 4 reserved nodes from dedicated spare pool to hosted-us-west1. Command:
```
infra scale pool hosted-us-west1 --add 4 --source reserved-spares
```
mike (infra): NVLink logs look noisy for node-infer-uw1-07 — driver reported transient timeouts around 1758002450. I'm pulling dmesg and nvlink diagnostics.
ana (sre): rolling traffic for cust-acme to fallback variant (model-prod-v1) via routing policy:
```
PATCH /api/route/cust-acme
{ "primary": "model-prod-v1", "failover": "model-prod-v2" }
```
customer-support: notified customers and requested session IDs and a sample problematic response. they sent back session ids: s-8723, s-8724.
oncall-rotation: after disabling batching and routing the customer, p95 dropped to ~340ms within 90s, p99 down to ~1.0s — improvement but not fully recovered.
ana (sre): streaming stalls still showing on those three workers. logs:
```
[1758002469] worker stream-03: send_pipeline blocked: waiting for socket flush, pending_out=62, last_send=1758002405
[1758002471] kv_cache: miss for key seq:1083; recompute took 2.1s
```
julie (runtime): hypothesis: a combination of long sequence recomputes + socket backpressure from a small number of slow clients is causing cumulative tail latency. next: isolate slow client connections and drop/shed them, enable backpressure mitigation (socket timeouts reduced), and ensure retry paths aren't flooding.
mike (infra): i've quarantined node-infer-uw1-07 from the pool (cordon) and restarted streaming process. heatmap shows node's memcpy stalls are gone after restart.
sam (eng-platform): applying socket timeout change and per-connection send window cap for streaming: 
```
PATCH /api/config/streaming
{ "send_timeout_s": 15, "max_pending_messages": 20 }
```
sam (eng-platform): change applied.
oncall-rotation: monitoring effects... p99 now ~650ms, p95 ~210ms. streaming stalls rate decreased ~80%.
ana (sre): still seeing KV cache churn for long sequences from cust-acme sessions. increasing kv-cache TTL to reduce churn (temp):
```
PATCH /api/cache/kv
{ "default_ttl_s": 3600 }
```
julie (runtime): TTL bumped — verifying hit rate.
mike (infra): node-infer-uw1-07 logs look good post-restart; no further NVLink errors. marking node healthy.
customer-support: informed customers of mitigation steps and asked for validation.
ana (sre): action items: 1) keep batching disabled for 15m and observe 2) keep reserved nodes online for 30m 3) collect traces for 1758002400-1758003000 for waveform analysis 4) follow up with cust-acme to see if they can throttle client-side tail behavior.
oncall-rotation: preparing incident record. severity: P2 (customer impact for a subset of sessions), pages escalated. taking ownership for next 2h shift.
julie (runtime): postmortem notes to collect: kernel NVLink anomalies on uw1-07, streaming socket backpressure patterns, kv-cache TTL misconfiguration coupled with large sequence workload, and model batching tuning that amplified tail.
sam (eng-platform): saved a snapshot of streaming workers and uploaded traces: https://traces.redwood.internal/trace/17580024x
ana (sre): thanks all. reopening runbook for a follow-up action: add guardrail to prevent batching auto-increase during sustained kv misses, and add a circuit-breaker to shed slow streaming clients earlier.
oncall-rotation: marking incident as mitigated for now — will handoff to follow-up rotation. FINAL TIMELINE SNIPPET:
- 1758002400: initial p99 uptick
- 1758002420: kv-cache misses spike
- 1758002435: NVLink transient on node-infer-uw1-07
- 1758002450: batching disabled; route changed for cust-acme
- 1758002500: reserved nodes added; node restart
- 1758002580: socket timeout tweak + TTL bump
- 1758002700: p95/p99 back to acceptable range (monitoring)

incidents-bot: Incident recorded #INC-2026-462. Follow-up assigned to runtime/infra for postmortem and to platform for runbook updates. :white_check_mark:
